title: EPF ECR filing and contribution payment
summary: Upload the monthly UAN-based Electronic Challan-cum-Return on the EPFO employer portal and remit EPF, EPS and EDLI contributions plus administrative charges for the previous wage month.
applicability: Establishments covered by Chapter III of the Code on Social Security 2020 (20 or more employees, or voluntarily covered). Membership is mandatory for employees whose PF wages are within the wage ceiling: Rs 15,000 per month up to 16 Sep 2026 and Rs 25,000 per month from 17 Sep 2026 (S.O. 5109(E)).
law: Section 16 and Chapter III, Code on Social Security 2020; Employees' Provident Fund Scheme 2026, Employees' Pension Scheme 2026 and EDLI Scheme 2026 (notified 29 Jun 2026, replacing the EPF Scheme 1952, EPS 1995 and EDLI Scheme 1976); Sections 127, 128 and 133 of the Code
penalty: Simple interest at 12% per annum from the due date (Section 127; S.O. 2698(E), deemed from 21 Nov 2025). Damages under Section 128 up to the amount of arrears, reported under the 2026 Scheme as 0.25% per month for delays up to 2 months, 0.50% for 2-4 months and 1% beyond 4 months. A late return reportedly attracts Rs 500 per day, capped at that month's administrative charges. Non-payment is an offence under Section 133 (1-3 years and a Rs 1 lakh fine where the employee share deducted is not paid).

other: Damages u/s 128 up to 100% of arrears (reported graded rate 0.25%-1% per month by length of delay)
Late-return fee capped at the month's administrative charges (variable, so no fixed cap)
Prosecution u/s 133: imprisonment 1-3 years and Rs 1 lakh fine if the deducted employee share is not remitted

title: Tamil Nadu LWF annual contribution
summary: Annual contribution for each employee on the register on 31 December: Rs 20 employee share (recovered from the December or last wages) and Rs 40 employer share, paid to the Tamil Nadu Labour Welfare Board before 31 January of the next year.
applicability: Factories, motor transport undertakings, plantations, catering establishments and other establishments (including societies and trusts) employing 5 or more persons on any day in the preceding 12 months; employees who worked at least 30 days in the year, excluding managerial staff, supervisors drawing over Rs 15000 a month, apprentices and part-time workers.
law: Section 15, Tamil Nadu Labour Welfare Fund Act 1972; Rules 11-A and 12(1), Tamil Nadu Labour Welfare Fund Rules 1973 (Rule 11-A rates amended by G.O. Ms. No. 161, Labour Welfare and Skill Development (G2), 2 Dec 2022)
penalty: The Act copy reviewed has no specific late-payment interest on contributions (the S.14 penal interest of 1 percent then 1.5 percent per month covers unpaid accumulations and fines); unpaid sums are recoverable as arrears of land revenue under S.28, and obstruction or non-production of records is an offence under S.29.

other: Recoverable as arrears of land revenue (S.28)
Prosecution possible for obstructing inspection or not producing records (S.29)
exposure.basis: TN LWF Act 1972: S.28 land-revenue recovery; S.14 interest applies to unpaid accumulations and fines, not expressly to contributions.

title: Telangana LWF annual contribution
summary: Annual contribution of Rs 2 per employee (employee share) and Rs 5 per employee (employer share) for employees on the register as of 31 December, paid to the Welfare Commissioner with a Form F statement by 31 January of the next year.
applicability: Factories, motor transport undertakings, and shops or establishments (including societies and trusts) employing 20 or more persons on any day in the preceding 12 months; employees engaged for 30 days in 12 months, excluding managerial staff and supervisors drawing over Rs 1600 a month.
law: Section 10, Telangana Labour Welfare Fund Act 1987 (AP Act 34 of 1987 as adapted by G.O.Ms.No.6, LET&F (Labour), 1 Feb 2016); Rule 6, Telangana Labour Welfare Fund Rules 1988
penalty: No specific late-payment interest on contributions in the Act (S.9 penal interest of 1 percent then 1.5 percent per month covers unpaid accumulations and fines). Under Rule 8 the Welfare Commissioner can serve a 15-day demand notice, and dues are recoverable as arrears of land revenue (S.24); obstruction or non-production of records is punishable under S.25.

Fine up to Rs 500 or 3 months imprisonment for obstruction or non-production of records (S.25)

title: West Bengal LWF half-yearly contribution
summary: For each employee on the register, Rs 3 employee share and Rs 30 employer share (Rs 33 in all) for each half-year ending 30 June and 31 December, paid online on the Board portal (lwf.wblabour.gov.in) before 15 July and 15 January.
applicability: Factories, tramway or motor transport undertakings, commercial establishments that employed 10 or more persons in the preceding 12 months, and other notified classes (the Board lists plantations, hotels, restaurants and entertainment establishments); managerial staff and higher-paid supervisors are excluded.
law: Section 9(2)-(6), West Bengal Labour Welfare Fund Act 1974 (S.9(2) substituted by WB Act XLVI of 2017 - rates notified by the State; S.9(6) online payment by WB Act XI of 2023); West Bengal Labour Welfare Fund Rules 1976
penalty: S.10: after a demand notice, simple interest of 1 percent of the dues per complete month for the first three months and 1.5 percent per month thereafter (remittable). S.21(2): failure to pay contribution is punishable - imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to Rs 2000 in the original text; WB Act XI of 2023 replaces this with a fine up to Rs 50000 once notified.

other: Interest rises to 1.5 percent per month after the first three months; only after a demand notice
S.21(2) original text: imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to Rs 2000 for failing to pay contribution

title: Plastic packaging EPR annual return (PIBOs)

summary: Producers, importers and brand owners of plastic packaging file an annual return on the CPCB EPR portal on plastic packaging placed on the market and plastic packaging waste collected and processed against their EPR targets, including recycled content and EPR certificates used.
applicability: PIBOs registered under the Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 - with CPCB if operating in more than two States/UTs, otherwise with the SPCB/PCC - for all categories of plastic packaging.

Registration may be suspended or revoked; closure of operations for unregistered PIBOs

title: E-waste EPR annual return (CPCB portal)

title: FSSAI annual return (Form D-1) on FoSCoS
summary: Licensed food manufacturers and importers file an online annual return on FoSCoS, separately for each licence, covering every class of food product handled in the previous financial year.
applicability: Holders of a State or Central FSSAI licence who manufacture (including repackers and relabellers), import, or manufacture for export. Registration (basic) holders are not covered. From 1 April 2026 FSSAI revised the thresholds (registration up to Rs 1.5 crore turnover, State licence above Rs 1.5 crore up to Rs 50 crore, Central licence above Rs 50 crore), so manufacturers that migrate to registration should fall outside D-1.
law: Regulation 2.1.13, Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations 2011, as applied by FSSAI orders dated 18-12-2020 and 10-11-2022; Regulation 2.1.7(2) as substituted by the FSS (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Amendment Regulations 2026 (notified 10-03-2026)
penalty: Rs 100 per day from 1 June until filing, capped at 5 times the annual licence fee (FSSAI order dated 10-11-2022, applicable from FY 2021-22); FSSAI has said waiver requests will not be considered. Under regulation 2.1.7(2) as substituted on 10-03-2026, a licence is deemed suspended while the return is outstanding after the due date, no food business may be carried on during suspension, and the suspension ends once the return is filed with the penalty.

other: Late fee capped at 5 times the annual licence fee (FSSAI order 10-11-2022)
Licence deemed suspended until the return is filed with the late fee (reg 2.1.7(2), from 10-03-2026)
Revised return after 31 May costs one or two years of licence fee plus GST (FSSAI order 08-01-2024)

title: Bulk waste generator annual return (SWM Rules 2026)
form: Annual return on the centralised solid waste portal
summary: Bulk waste generators file an annual return on the centralised online portal on their Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility (EBWGR) obligation, including EBWGR certificates procured for the solid waste they generate.
applicability: Bulk waste generators under the Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 - institutional and other listed users such as government departments, PSUs, private companies and educational institutions - whose premises have a floor area of 20,000 sq m or more, or water use of 40,000 litres per day, or waste generation of 100 kg per day. They must also register with the local body on the portal.
law: Rule 6(a) and 6(h), Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 (S.O. 388(E) dated 27-01-2026), in force 1-04-2026; rule 17 (environmental compensation)
penalty: Environmental compensation levied by the SPCB/PCC on the polluter-pays principle under rule 17 and CPCB guidelines; rule 17(5) keeps action under the EP Act available in addition.

other: Environmental compensation per CPCB guidelines under rule 17
Action under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986 in addition (rule 17(5))
